title: Joint Health Assessment in von Willebrand Disease
summary:
Von Willebrand disease (vWD) is the most common inherited bleeding disorder and is caused by a deficiency or dysfunction of the von Willebrand factor. While joint bleeding and the resulting permanent joint damage (arthropathy) are well studied in classical
hemophilia, data on the frequency of joint impairment in vWD remain insufficient. However, estimates suggest that approximately one in four patients with moderate to severe VWD is also affected by joint bleeding, which may result in chronic pain and limitations in mobility and daily activities.
The aim of this study is to assess joint health in patients with vWD and to gain initial insights into the frequency and severity of joint damage, which are necessary for planning future larger studies. The study will also examine how joint health affects patients’ daily lives.
Over a period of two years, the joint status of 40 to 50 patients with von Willebrand disease and von Willebrand factor activity < 30% will be examined using a combination of different
diagnostic methods and patient questionnaires. These include a physical examination of the joints, ultrasound imaging, and the use of specialized questionnaires in which patients evaluate their limitations in daily activities, existing pain, and quality of life.
